summary: Five experiments completed in 0.7 minutes, including three compute-bound tasks. The 0.64-minute Repaired provenance-complete live belief shadow trace was the longest entry, but no data available this milestone explains why; the locked compute-task idle indicator is false.
bottlenecks_identified: The Repaired provenance-complete live belief shadow trace consumed 0.64 of the 0.7 recorded minutes, but no phase-level data is available to attribute that time.
Disk-mtime reconstruction reports the other entries between 0.0 and 0.02 minutes, which is too coarse to separate execution cost from artifact bookkeeping.
No data available this milestone identifies model cardinality or runner dispatch, so eligibility for parallel multi-model execution cannot be audited.
improvements_suggested: Record monotonic start, end, and phase timings in every experiment artifact so the critical path has a causal breakdown.
Capture task-scoped GPU utilization across each compute-bound execution window instead of relying on an uncorrelated idle snapshot.
Record model count and runner selection at launch, and select DualGPURunner only when multiple models are loaded in parallel.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Add per-phase monotonic timing to experiment artifacts.
Add task-window GPU telemetry for compute-bound experiments.
Add model-count and runner-dispatch metadata with conditional DualGPURunner selection for parallel multi-model tasks.
meta_reflection: The reconstructed timing identifies the critical path but not its cause. Better task-window timing, GPU, model-count, and dispatch telemetry would make the next retrospective causal without misclassifying synthesis-only idleness.
